purpose: Landmark-compatible scapular audit to resolve the earlier GH-to-inferior-angle measurement conflict without relying on incompatible scapular-height definitions.

landmark_mapping.a003_AA: ISB acromial angle / posterolateral acromial reference used by the master
landmark_mapping.a003_TS: trigonum spinae / medial root of scapular spine
landmark_mapping.source_d3: posterolateral corner of acromion to midpoint of medial border of scapular spine
landmark_mapping.compatibility: AA-to-TS is a close anatomical match to source d3; retain moderate mapping confidence because wording is not literally identical.

male_d4_superior_to_inferior_angle_mm.warning: Does not map directly to a003 AA-to-AI or GH-to-AI.

findings: The earlier GH-to-inferior-angle comparison was correctly withdrawn because its measurement definition did not match published scapular height.

A better landmark-compatible test now directly confirms the transverse scapular problem: a003 AA-to-TS is ~227 mm, while a male 3D-CT sample reports ~113±6.6 mm (observed range 90-129 mm) for the posterolateral acromion to medial scapular-spine midpoint distance.

The a003 value is ~17.3 SD above that male mean and ~98 mm beyond the observed male maximum in the cited sample. Even allowing for imperfect AA/TS wording equivalence, this is too large to treat as normal anatomy.

Therefore the scapula can be upgraded from 'method-conflicted only' to a confirmed transverse/medial-border geometry defect. The exact superior-inferior length remains open because AA/GH distances are not identical to superior-angle-to-inferior-angle measurements.
This aligns with the independent shoulder-width finding: the old mesh forced both clavicle and scapula too far laterally.
canonical_actions: Retarget AA/TS (acromial angle to scapular-spine root) into a male adult corridor before fitting the mesh.
Add spinoglenoid and suprascapular notch reference landmarks so d6/d7/d8 can be tested directly.
Keep superior-angle and inferior-angle targets separate from AA/GH spans; do not reuse vertical-height evidence for oblique distances.
After the local scapular frame is built, place glenoid/GH, coracoid, acromion and medial border consistently and rerun shoulder movement tests.
hard_tests: AA-to-TS must fall within a multi-source adult-male or stature-adjusted corridor; current a003 is explicitly rejected.
AA/TS/AI must form a nondegenerate 3D scapular plane.
AC and GH remain distinct and lie on anatomically correct acromion/glenoid structures.
Scapular neutral orientation is applied only after source frame angles are transformed into the HGPT basis.
